name: Dutch Stroopwafel
description: Stroopwafel, a caramel-filled waffle cookie, genuinely began as a resourceful use of bakery leftovers in 18th-century Gouda - real technique splits the waffle open with a knife the moment it comes off the iron, since waiting even a minute lets it crisp up and become impossible to cut cleanly.

ingredients_full.note: tbsp, standing in for stroop syrup

ingredients.note: tbsp, standing in for stroop syrup

steps_detailed: Mix the flour, softened butter, baking powder, sugar, and egg into a firm dough.
Divide into small balls and cook one at a time in a hot waffle iron, about 90 seconds, until golden.

The instant each waffle comes off the iron, slice it horizontally with a sharp knife while still hot - real technique depends on doing this immediately, before it crisps and becomes impossible to split cleanly.
Spread the warm honey inside and press the two halves back together.

name: Dutch Hutspot
description: Hutspot, a real stamppot variation of mashed potato with carrot and onion, is a genuine Dutch winter staple, real technique boiling everything together in the same pot and mashing it as one, not serving the vegetables on the side.
steps_detailed: Boil the potato, carrot, and onion together in the same pot until all completely tender, 18-20 minutes.
Drain and mash everything together with the butter and milk - real hutspot is mashed as one dish, not kept separate.

name: Dutch Bitterballen
description: Bitterballen, deep-fried breaded meat balls, genuinely began as a way to use up leftover ragout stew - real technique double-coats each ball in egg and breadcrumbs for a real extra-crunchy exterior around the creamy filling.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef, 6-7 minutes.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour, cook 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the broth until thickened into a real ragout.
Stir the beef into the ragout, then chill at least 1 hour until firm enough to shape.
Shape into small balls, then dip in the egg and breadcrumbs, and repeat a second time for a real extra-crunchy coating.
Deep-fry at 350F (175C) for 4-5 minutes until deeply golden.

name: Dutch Erwtensoep (Split Pea Soup)
description: Erwtensoep, a genuinely thick split pea soup, is a real Dutch winter staple, real technique simmering the peas long enough that they break down completely and thicken the soup naturally.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Peas, split, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt

ingredients.ingredient: Peas, split, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt

steps_detailed: Cook the onion and carrot 4-5 minutes.
Add the split peas and broth, and simmer 25-30 minutes, until the peas break down completely and the soup thickens naturally.
steps: Cook the onion and carrot 4-5 minutes.
Add the split peas and broth, and simmer 25-30 minutes, until the peas break down completely and the soup thickens naturally.

name: Dutch Poffertjes
description: Poffertjes, small, fluffy yeasted pancakes, are a beloved Dutch treat, real technique using real yeast for a genuine light rise, cooked in a special pan with small indentations.

ingredients_full.note: melted, plus more for the pan

ingredients.note: melted, plus more for the pan

steps_detailed: Whisk the flour, baking powder, egg, milk, and melted butter into a smooth, thin batter.
Let rest 15-20 minutes.
Cook small spoonfuls in a well-buttered pan (or standard pan if a poffertjes pan isn't available), 2-3 minutes per side, until golden.
Dust with powdered sugar before serving.

name: Dutch Pea Soup Sausage
description: Rookworst, smoked sausage, is the real, traditional protein simmered directly in or served alongside erwtensoep and stamppot.
steps_detailed: Simmer or grill the sausage, turning, 10-12 minutes, until heated through and lightly browned.
steps: Simmer or grill the sausage, turning, 10-12 minutes, until heated through and lightly browned.

name: Dutch Cucumber Salad
description: A simple vinegar-dressed cucumber salad, a common Dutch side, real technique salting the cucumber first to draw out excess water.
steps_detailed: Salt the cucumber slices and let sit 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Whisk the vinegar, oil, and sugar together, and toss with the cucumber.

name: Dutch Roasted Almonds
description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across the Netherlands.
steps_detailed: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Dutch home cooking outside the specific named dishes.

Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.
